title: EDDS / DDID – Presentation & Demo
short_title: EDDS / DDID presentation and demo (Solar Orbiter)
status_notes: Title slide dated 28/09/2017; slide 2 states it was updated by Paula Margarido for Solar Orbiter (January 2019). The file name gives 'SOL-ESC-PRS-22100, Is.1, Rev.0, 20190130', which is not printed on the slides.
summary:
An 80-slide ESOC training presentation, 'EDDS / DDID – Presentation & Demo', first given on 28 September 2017 by Daniel Werner (Mission Data Systems Manager for BepiColombo) and Rui Santos (Technical Officer for EDDS), and updated by Paula Margarido for Solar Orbiter in January 2019. It introduces external users (instrument teams and the Science Ground Segment) to the Solar Orbiter Data Delivery Interface Control Document (DDID) and to the EGOS Data Dissemination System (EDDS).

The DDID part gives the document status (issue 1.0 of 2013, issue 1.2 expected in mid 2019), its relation to the generic EDDS External User ICD (issue 15.0, February 2018), how change records and attached XML schema files are provided, and the relevant chapters. The EDDS part explains its purpose (controlled access to mission data for users without MCS access), the archives it reads (PARC, DARC, FARC and file system), what it is not (a data warehouse or analysis tool), client baselines, the web, Java Web Start and standalone clients, security (LDAP users, roles, data access and quota sets, HTTPS, SFTP, AES encryption), batch and stream services and delivery options, and the architecture (EUD-based client, Tomcat web server, EDDS server, delivery manager).

A long section walks through the client user interface with example requests, then lists every batch request type (PARC TM/TC/event raw, report, gap and statistics requests, out-of-limits reports, DARC parameter requests, FARC and file-system requests) and the response formats (ProtoBuf binary, EDDS Raw, GDDS Binary, XML, XSLT transform, ASCII), together with the SCOS-2000 packet header concept. It ends with good practice (compression, file-split naming), recommendations (packet reports with raw data, ProtoBuf), and a questionnaire on network and SFTP/GFTS set-up.

key_points.text: The Solar Orbiter DDID complements the generic EDDS External User ICD (EGOS-GEN-EDDS-ICD-1001, issue 15.0 of 2018/02/16); at the time, DDID issue 1.0 (2013/09/10) was current and issue 1.2 was expected in mid 2019, issue 1.1 having been internal only.
XML schema files are attached to the DDID PDF as a ZIP file with a dummy '.removeThisExtension' suffix to by-pass PDF reader security.

EDDS provides controlled access to mission data for users without access to the MCS, by retrieving data from PARC (packets), DARC (parameters), FARC (files) and the file system; it keeps backward-compatible interfaces of its predecessors GDDS and TDRS.
EDDS is not a data warehouse (response files are stored only for a limited time) and not a post-processing or analysis tool.

EDDS users are authenticated against an LDAP server; access is based on user roles, data access sets, operation data sets and quota sets; HTTPS and SFTP are used and AES encryption of data is supported.

EDDS components: an EUD-based client, an Apache Tomcat web server (HTTPS/SOAP portal and authentication), the EDDS server (authorisation, quota, retrieval, filtering, formatting, compression, encryption) and a delivery manager.
'Packet TM' returns raw source packets without extra headers, while 'Packet TM Raw PARC data' returns the full SCOS-2000 packet with common and TM headers; 'Packet TC Report' is the TC history.
The out-of-limits record report shows only raw values, not engineering values.

Response formats are Binary (Google ProtoBuf or physical files), EDDS Raw (ASCII hex string), GDDS Binary, XML (with XSLT transform) and ASCII; ProtoBuf is described as the best-performing format, and framed messages are length-prefixed.
Recommendations: use 'Pkt Reports' including raw data, and the Binary (ProtoBuf) response format whenever possible; request zip or tar.gz compression.

notes: Source is a PowerPoint (.pptx) file, so there are no PDF pages: srcgrep reports every match as p.1. In this record every pdf_page value is the slide number (slides 1 to 80, in presentation order, verified against the slide list in the file). Many slides are screenshots of the EDDS client with little text (slides 22-41). Slide 5 prints the DDID reference as 'BC-ESC-IF-05011', whereas the DDID itself (library item solo-ddid-i1r2) prints 'SOL-ESC-IF-05011'. Slide 48 lists Solar Orbiter custom field names in a table that the text extraction reduces to '0'. Slide 59 is a hex dump of an example ProtoBuf response. The document ID and date in the file name (SOL-ESC-PRS-22100, Is.1, Rev.0, 2019-01-30) are not printed on the slides.
